  4105. >341</button>
  4106. <span class="git-code-text">&lt;p&gt;To deliver the Doc and increase the chance of target opening it, we have to use a convincing pretext and an alternate delivery method. A download link for example.&lt;/p&gt;</span>
  4107. </li>
  4109. ​
  4110. <li class="git-code-line" id="L342" data-git-line="342">
  4111. <button
  4112. type="button"

  4116. title="Copy permalink for line 342"
  4117. >342</button>
  4118. <span class="git-code-text">&lt;p&gt;If succesfully delivered and opened, the doc will be tagged with the &lt;a href=&quot;https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1553/005/&quot;&gt;&amp;quot;Mark of the Web&amp;quot; (MOTW)&lt;/a&gt;. An Office doc tagged with MOTW will open in a &lt;a href=&quot;https://support.office.com/en-us/article/what-is-protected-view-d6f09ac7-e6b9-4495-8e43-2bbcdbcb6653&quot;&gt;protected view&lt;/a&gt; which disabled editing and blocks the execution of macros or embedded objects. When a target opens a MOTW Doc, they see a warning with the option to Enable Editing.&lt;/p&gt;</span>
  4119. </li>
  4121. ​
  4122. <li class="git-code-line" id="L343" data-git-line="343">

  4128. title="Copy permalink for line 343"
  4129. >343</button>
  4130. <span class="git-code-text">&lt;p&gt;When the target enables editing, the protected view is disabled. The most direct way to bypass MOTW is to convince the target to click Enable Editing.&lt;/p&gt;</span>
  4131. </li>

  4226. <span class="git-code-text">&lt;p&gt;Microsoft also announced blocking macros by default. Affecting Access, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio, and Word in most Office versions from 2013-2021. Dates can be found in &lt;a href=&quot;https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployoffice/security/internet-macros-blocked&quot;&gt;MS Learn page&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;</span>

  4237. >352</button>
  4238. <span class="git-code-text">&lt;p&gt;The Enable Content button is no longer available for Office docs delivered from the internet. A more tedious process of following a link outlining the dangers, following instructions, and checking a box in settings. This complicated the vector, but with thorough enumeration and considering the information here the chance of success increases greatly.&lt;/p&gt;</span>
  4239. </li>
  4241. ​
  4242. <li class="git-code-line" id="L353" data-git-line="353">

  4249. >353</button>
  4250. <span class="git-code-text">&lt;p&gt;Despite the mitigation and heightened awareness, malicious Office Docs are still one of the most widely used client-side attack vectors. This highlights the dynamic between attacker and defender. For each security measure implemented the attacker is forced to develop a novel vectors and bypass methods. New defense mechanisms are just opportunities to develop more sophisticated attacks.&lt;/p&gt;</span>
  4251. </li>

  4284. title="Copy permalink for line 356"
  4285. >356</button>
  4286. <span class="git-code-text">&lt;li&gt;Office apps like Word and Excel allow users to embed macros.&lt;ul&gt;</span>
  4287. </li>

  4311. </li>
  4313. ​

  4346. <span class="git-code-text">&lt;li&gt;&lt;em&gt;Macros can be written from scratch in &lt;a href=&quot;https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/office/vba/api/overview/&quot;&gt;Visual Basic for Applications (VBA)&lt;/a&gt;, which is a powerful scripting language with full access to &lt;a href=&quot;https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ActiveX&quot;&gt;ActiveX objects&lt;/a&gt; and the Windows Script Host, similar to JavaScript in HTML Applications.&lt;/em&gt;.&lt;/li&gt;</span>
  4347. </li>
  4349. ​

  4370. <span class="git-code-text">&lt;p&gt;Example; we will embed a macro in a Word doc to launch a reverse shell when the document is opened. Macros are one of the oldest and most well known attack vectors and still work well today, keeping in mind the mitigation described in the previous section.&lt;/p&gt;</span>
  4371. </li>
  4373. ​
